Last semester I made it so I only had classes MWF. So, I ended up working 13 hour shifts on Tuesday and thursday. Along with some night shifts after class whenever they needed. I also took an English class online to make room. All in all, it was hectic being a full time student and working a full time job. But, I felt accomplished that I could manage it.

Online classes whenever possible, it saves you money on gas and it saves you the time you would spend driving, plus some classes are just less time consuming online. In-person classes should be taken at times that you don't expect to be working much, if at all.

Should note that it would be good to check for the cost difference of gas saved and cost for taking online classes. When I graduated attended University there was an additional charge per credit for online classes that made it way more expensive to take online classes then on campus classes. I ended up having to take a few when I was doing my internships or when my schedule wouldn't allow for me to take that class on campus. If it does cost more just weight out the cost vs reward of taking an online class. If you would be able to make more money by not having to go to that class and working then do it.

My dad has always wanted a kitten. However, at the shelter, there are 50 cats in need of a home. I want to surprise him this Sunday with a companion, but I feel guilty with choosing a kitten that will have a bigger chance at finding a home rather than a slightly older cat.
Why Do People Opt to Get Kittens Rather Than Older Cats?

Kittens are cute and harmless (no bad habits yet, unlikely to be feral). You also get a sense of growing as an owner, along with your pet. You both mature together as owner and beloved pet.

The same thing can be applied to human adoption as well. People are more likely to want to adopt younger children, than older ones.

It is just human nature.

cuteness is a big factor for a lot of people. Although lots of people adopt kittens and puppies in order to train them, without having to untrain many bad behaviors previous owners may have instilled into them.
I opted for kittens because I wanted to help guide behavioral development.
Because I knew I'd get attached and wanted as long as possible with my baby.
They taste better and the meat is more tender. . .(no wonder I get down votes—completely suck at awareness)

If your dad is a decent person (I'm not implying that he isn't), then get him an older cat, and explain why. You are definitely right in feeling that way, A LOT of older animals end up never finding a home, because everyone wants a kitten/puppy.

I just knocked over every cat at the shelter to find the least aggressive one and adopted it. I did get a kitten (7 months old when we adopted her), but it worked out better to have a kitten with my daughter since she was so young. My cat is very tolerant of her (had Sugar for 2 1/2 years now).
lol cat tipping as a selection tool, I like it.

It sounds awful, but anyone who has kids know how they are with animals lol. They aren't as gentle with them as we'd like until they get older so I figured whatever cat would just take it and not attack was the right one. My cat basically has the perfect personality for kids.

I don't think it sounds awful at all, though personally I would go for a cat that responds, but gently, to indicate its annoyance.

My reasoning being that it will help the child learn empathy more quickly; one cannot really understand that one is hurting another without being hurt. I wouldn't want the kid to get scratched badly, but a little emotional pain from the shock of being bopped can help one get with the program a little quicker, imo.

Kitten is something I think everyone should experience once. Cats from the shelter are so thankful in their cat way. Any cat I get in the future will be from the shelter. Normally the shelters will have kittens but they are not out front to encourage adoption of the older cars.

I've never owned a car until a few weeks ago and I think older cats are the way to go.

Sure, people choose kittens because they want to shape them behaviorally, but you can do that with older cats too. Kittens are cute, but older cats can be cute too. I think my cat is cute every single day. I prefer older cats because they have a harder time of being adopted, they're normally cheaper to adopt and they're better if you can't devote the time needed for young pets.

I wouldn't feel guilty. Kitten or cat, you are finding an unwanted pet a good (hopefully permanent) home. Unwanted animals are a sad thing to see but it's not your fault as long as you don't contribute to the problem, and spay/neuter your pets, even if they are indoor pets.

With regards to a cat or kitten, I would get a cat if you want a specific personality. I would get a kitten if watching the development of your pet is more important than getting a specific "type" of cat personality. Kittens' personalities change so you never know what kind of adult you'll get. Also if you get a kitten, I would recommend getting another as a play companion, and to also help the kitten learn how to interact with other cats.

I prefer adopting cats, not kittens. I agree that you can help shape the personality of a dog/puppy...but I think cats are going to be what they are going to be, no matter how old you get them or how you try to 'train' them.

My ex bought a kitten. She was a bitch as a kitten, and even though we loved her and spoiled her she was a bitch as a cat. Seriously one of the meanest cats I have ever encountered. A few years ago I adopted a 6 y/o cat from the SPCA and he is the sweetest, most chill cat ever. I could tell he was chill when I saw him, and when they put him on the floor of their meeting room he trotted right to me and started rubbing up on my legs. Now he follows me around like a dog.

But people like kittens. They are adorable.

My last four cats have been rescue cats, with the youngest being 10 months. I am down to two (I never have more than two at a time, and lost the first two of the four to cancer and a stroke).

If you are going with a kitten, consider a black kitten, because black cats statistically do not get adopted as easily. My 10 month boy had been In a no-kill rescue since birth, and he kept getting passed over due to his color. He is three now and is the sweetest, most affectionate cat with no bad habits whatsoever. He is also huge because he is a Maine Coon mix.
